sentences.text:
This writ petition is filed by the petitioners seeking following reliefs:
"10.1.

That, the Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to direct the respondents not to take possession or use the lands of petitioners situated at khasra no.101/9, 101/6,
101/8, 101/2 admeasuring total 1.598 hectares, kourinbhata Patwari Halka No.24,
Ward Number 19 Ramkrishna Ward, Tehsil and District- Rajnandgaron without acquiring the same under the provision of the Act of 2013.

10.2. That, Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to direct the respondents to act as provision of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement act 2013.

entities.text: Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement act 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 10.3. That Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to direct the respondents to pay the compensation to the petitioners for illegal harassment.

10.4. Or in alternate direct the respondents to initiate the proceeding for the acquisition of petitioners lands and compensation and damages be paid to the petitioners, till than possession of the petitioners may not disturb."
10.5.
Any other relief/relief, which this Hon'ble Court may think fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case, may also please be granted to the petitioner."

2. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that respondent Municipal Corporation have demolished the boundary-wall erected by them and further issued notice to petitioners stating therein that the petitioners have encroached upon Govt. land.

It is contended that petitioners have earlier filed writ petition bearing WPC No.1907 2014 which was disposed of observing that first,
demarcation to be conducted and if upon demarcation it is found that petitioners are not encroachers and are in possession of their own land and land of petitioners is required for widening of road, then respondent Corporation shall draw appropriate acquisition proceeding.
It is contention of learned counsel for the petitioners that after passing of order, demarcation was done and on that date it is reported that petitioners were in possession of land owned by them.
Thereafter the land as on date is lying open and is used by other private persons as road.

He submits that based on the order passed in WPC No.1907 of 2014, Municipal Corporation wrote letter to the Land Acquisition Officer for acquisition of the land admeasuring 221.56 sq.ft bearing kh. no.101/2 and have tentatively computed amount of compensation which is required to be paid to land owners.
However, till date amount of compensation is not paid.
3. Learned counsel for the respondent - Municipal Corporation submits that submission of learned counsel for the petitioners is not correct.
Acquisition proceedings for acquiring land of the petitioners has not been initiated.

He also submits that in the year 2014 itself, letter was written by the Corporation to the petitioners mentioning that land measuring 2384 sq.ft. bearing kh. no.101/2 will be required for widening of existing 60 feet road.
Proposed road is mentioned in the Master Plan issued by Town and Country Planning Department.

The letter further clarifies that if the private land of petitioners is to be used, appropriate proceedings for land acquisition computing Smt. Rashmi Gauri Bhojani vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 17 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104346287/
2 amount of compensation will be initiated.

entities.text: Rashmi Gauri Bhojani vs State Of Chhattisgarh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He also contended that as of now Corporation has not constructed any road and the petitioners are free to use their private ownership land.
4. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and also perused the documents annexed along with writ petition.

5. Corporation has placed on record the documents including letter dated 04.12.2014 (Annexure R-3/4) addressed to petitioner No.1 specifying that the land owned by the petitioners may be required in future for widening of the proposed road as per Master Plan published by the Town and Country Panning Department and if land of the petitioners is utilized for road, compensation will be calculated and paid after its acquisition.
Till date land owned by the petitioners is lying vacant and open.

6. In the aforementioned facts of he case, writ petition is disposed of based on submission of learned counsel for the respondent No.3/Corporation that the petitioners are free to use their private ownership land for their personal use as per the permission granted in the order of diversion.
